claims.text: The Data Science lane's tasks for FEAT-ZD-48600 are TSK-03 (STORY-03) and TSK-04 (STORY-04), both in ap_forecast.
The permission table's tool registry says no secrets are required or granted for the ap_forecast repository.
TSK-03 vendor_risk is rule-based, with no LLM, no network and no models.json read. It relies on predict_delay_days, a pure function that uses only statistics.mean from the standard library.

build_explanation_request returns a dict with provider, model, max_tokens and messages taken from models.json or a passed config, and does not send it. The configured provider is acme-llm, so TSK-04 needs no provider credential in ap_forecast.

A search of the ap_forecast source and tests for secret, token, key, credential and environment-variable terms found only the max_tokens request parameter, in explain.py, models.json and tests/test_forecast.py.
The existing tests use an explicit config or the bundled models.json and call no provider. The planned test_vendor_risk_no_llm patches ap_forecast.explain.load_config to fail.
Sending the risk label to acme-llm waits on Architect confirmation (TQ-8), which gates release, not coding.

The repository runs CI with ci.py and has a main (released) branch and a dev (integration) branch. For local/CI, dev and main, the required and granted secrets are both empty, so no access request was raised.

open_questions: SSQ-1 (non-blocking): Which component sends the build_explanation_request payload to acme-llm, and who owns its credential? It is outside ap_forecast and outside the scope of TSK-03 and TSK-04. If ap_forecast ever calls the provider directly, DS-02 must be re-entered.
